calls.body: The Ducks are near the top of the league for shot volume, but the Panthers are one of the best at keeping shots away. We think the Ducks still get theirs.

calls.head: The Panthers’ edge in preventing dangerous shots
calls.body: The Panthers are near the top of the league for preventing dangerous shots, and the Ducks are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Panthers prevent dangerous shots better than the Ducks do.

calls.beyond: Florida usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Anaheim’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.1% against Florida) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

ANA.head: We gave Anaheim a 61% chance, and they delivered.

FLA.head: We gave Florida only a 39% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Anaheim’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Anaheim’s power play has been near the bottom of the league for years, and Florida has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Not tonight: 3 power-play goals on 4 chances. A power play like theirs against a kill like Florida’s scores 3 or more about once every 25 games.

surprises.head: Anaheim won against the run of play
surprises.body: With chances like these, Florida would win about 69 games in 100. Anaheim won anyway.

story.head: Dostál steals one
paras: The Panthers’ Brad Marchand played his first game of the season, after missing the first two. Cutter Gauthier got the scoring started for the Ducks on the power play late in the first. Carter Verhaeghe made it 1-1, 51 seconds later. Gauthier scored again on the power play early in the second to put the Ducks ahead 2-1. Marchand tied it 2-2 on the power play with 1:50 left. Mikael Granlund won it on the power play in overtime. Gauthier also had an assist. Leo Carlsson finished with three assists.

The Panthers had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Panthers win about seven in ten. Lukáš Dostál was the difference, stopping 29 of 31. Jacob Markström stopped 17 of 20 for the Cats.
Special teams did the work: the Ducks scored three power-play goals on four chances and killed all four Panthers power plays. The Ducks improved to 2-0-0, and the Panthers dropped to 1-0-2.

items.text: The Ducks won their home opener.
With Aleksander Barkov out, Marchand took his spot and scored.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
